title: Postmortem: SEV-2 Runtime kernel selection caused latency spike (2026-03-18)
author: Ethan Park
customer_impact: p95 latency increased by ~2.1x for a subset of long-context requests (8kk tokens) in eu-west. Error rate remained low (<0.3%), but SLO burn occurred.
summary: A new kernel selection heuristic preferred a kernel variant that performed poorly for a specific sequence length distribution on A100s, causing latency regressions.
timeline:
15:12 UTC: SLO burn alert for eu-west chat long-context bucket fired.
15:20 UTC: On-call compared perf-canary data and saw regression after runtime build 2026.03.18.0.
15:33 UTC: Disabled new heuristic via feature flag; kernel selection reverted.
15:45 UTC: Latency returned near baseline; continued monitoring.
16:08 UTC: Incident resolved.
root_cause: The heuristic used average sequence length rather than a percentile-based feature, leading it to select a kernel optimized for uniform 8k sequences. Real traffic had a bimodal distribution with heavy tail, making the choice suboptimal.
detection: SLO burn alert and perf-canary comparison.
mitigation: Feature-flag rollback of the heuristic and forced kernel selection to the prior stable variant for the affected pool.
what_went_well: Feature flags allowed rapid rollback without rebuild. Canary data provided quick correlation.
what_went_wrong: The heuristic change lacked traffic-representative validation for eu-west. Documentation did not specify the assumptions behind the new metric.
follow_ups: Update kernel selection model features to use p90 sequence length and tail weight (Serving Runtime; due 2026-04-10).
Add eu-west long-context perf-canary gating for runtime releases (Release Engineering; due 2026-04-01).
Document kernel selection assumptions and safe rollback steps (Serving Runtime; due 2026-04-05).
